newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhstan tells firms to send oil output to farms.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhstan tells firms to send oil output to farms.

text.p: firms to hand over output to the ailing farm sector, setting off alarm bells on Monday among Western oil executives who said their projects here may be affected.

Industry executives said the government had issued a secret decree in late March ordering state-owned oil firms and western companies producing oil in Kazakhstan under joint ventures to hand over crude to help the spring sowing campaign.
"This is a terrible thing," said the head of a western energy company in Kazakhstan who declined to be named.
"You sign a contract, you do the best you can and then suddenly they (the Kazakh government) drop something else on you."

The order affects western companies already pumping and refining crude in Kazakhstan. The only oil majors believed to be affected are Chevron Corp and Mobil Corp of the United States, which are working the vast Tengiz field in western Kazakhstan, executives said.
Alexander Korablin, spokesman for the Agriculture Ministry, told Reuters that farms urgently needed 350,000 tonnes of diesel fuel and 100,000 tonnes of gasoline.

"We need the fuel now," Korablin said, adding that negotiations with oil and gas companies at the end of last month had been tough. "We want to buy fuel with futures contracts based on this year's harvest," he said.
Korablin said state-owned oil enterprises had agreed to the contracts, under which crude oil would be sent to domestic refineries for processing in to diesel and gasoline.
He did not say what prices the state was willing to pay.
But western companies have raised an outcry and say they are fighting what they term forced requisitioning.
The right to export output is fundamental to the economics of producing oil in new markets like Kazakhstan, where domestic energy prices are a fraction of international levels.
Joint ventures account for increasing levels of Kazakhstan's total oil output.
"This could drive away a lot of people who are looking at deals at the moment," said the representative of a western oil major in Kazakhstan.
